newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen trap in narrow-range, JGBs end lower.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen trap in narrow-range, JGBs end lower.

text.p: SIMEX Japanese government bond (JGB) futures fell and the Euroyen futures were trapped in narrow-ranges on Friday amid continued worries over Japan's banking sector, dealers said.
Nagging concerns over Japan's ailing financial system, especially the future of Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB), was the highlight this week, they said.
"The market was plagued by the banking jitters that never seem to go away. Most players were sidelined but bought on dips due to these concerns," said a dealer with a European institution.
After trading to a low of 99.23 in the morning, December Euroyen edged up a tick to 99.24. Its previous IMM close was at 99.25. Turnover was light, around 3,125 lots.
September Euroyen was at 99.37 unchanged from its IMM close.
Dealers pegged immediate resistance for the September contract at 99.39-99.40.
March JGB ended lower at 126.20 after hitting a high at 126.40 on a turnover of 293 lots.
"Activity was on roll-overs. People were buying March and selling June," said the dealer with the European institution.
"The market was underpinned by short-covering in the cash market when March dipped to 125.96 yesterday following Yamazaki's comments," another dealer said.
Taku Yamazaki, policy chief of Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party, commented on using public funds to protect investors against debenture defaults early Thursday.
The remark triggered some diversion of funds away from the bond market into the stock market, dealers said.
Eurodollar futures were stable as dealers awaited the U.S. Producer Price Index (PPI) for January, due later on Friday.
Some dealers expected the PPI to show a mild rise of 0.3 percent.
September Eurodollars ended at 94.29 against its previous IMM close of 94.28.
